subject: General Knowledge
description: Region-craft pairs, signature techniques, GI overlap, niche under-asked items

questions.stem: 'Pashmina' shawls — woven from the fine undercoat of the Changthangi goat — are a signature craft of:
questions.explanation: Pashmina — luxury wool from the Changthangi (Pashmina) goat that lives at altitudes above 4,500 m in the Changthang plateau (Ladakh) and adjoining Tibet. Wool is hand-spun, dyed and woven in Kashmir Valley. GI tag: Kashmir Pashmina (2008). The 'Kani' shawl (Kashmiri kani-kaar weaving) and 'Sozni' (needle embroidery) are sub-categories. Highest-quality pashmina passes the 'ring test' — the entire shawl can be drawn through a finger ring.

questions.stem: 'Bidriware' — ornamental metal ware with silver inlay on a blackened zinc-copper alloy base — originates from:
questions.explanation: Bidri — named after Bidar town (Karnataka, formerly part of Hyderabad State). 14th-century Bahmani Sultanate origin. Process: (1) cast a zinc-copper alloy (95:5) base; (2) engrave the design; (3) inlay pure silver wire / sheet; (4) treat with paste of soil (special Bidar soil + ammonium chloride) → permanent matte black background highlighting the silver. GI tag 2006. Moradabad — brassware. Tanjavur — Tanjore paintings + plates. Surat — zari embroidery.

questions.stem: 'Phulkari' — floral embroidery on a coarse cotton chunni / shawl — is associated with which state?
questions.explanation: Phulkari (Punjabi: 'flower work') — coarse cotton khaddar base + dense darning-stitch embroidery in untwisted silk floss (pat). Bagh = the densest variant where the entire fabric is covered in embroidery. Traditionally made by Punjabi/Haryanvi women for weddings and dowries. GI tag 2010 (Punjab). Other related crafts: chamba rumal (Himachal), kantha (West Bengal/Odisha), kasuti (Karnataka).

questions.stem: Which Odisha craft produces intricately appliqued canopies and umbrellas, traditionally for the Jagannath Temple's Rath Yatra?
questions.explanation: Pipili — small village 20 km from Puri — famous for vibrant cloth appliqué work. Brightly coloured fabric pieces are cut into shapes and stitched onto a base cloth, producing canopies (chandua), umbrellas, wall hangings, lampshades. Used during the Rath Yatra — the chariot canopies are made in Pipili. GI tag 2024. Other Odisha crafts: Patachitra (cloth scroll painting); Dhokra (lost-wax bell-metal — also Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, WB); Pattachitra Tussar Painting; Sambalpuri Ikat textiles.

questions.stem: Match craft with state — which pairing is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Pattachitra is from ODISHA (and West Bengal) — not Bihar. Bihar is famous for Madhubani / Mithila painting. Channapatna toys — wooden lacquer toys from Channapatna, Karnataka. Kalamkari — block-printed and hand-painted cotton textile from AP/Telangana (Srikalahasti and Machilipatnam styles). Warli — tribal mural style of the Warli tribe of Maharashtra (Thane/Palghar). Common exam-trap: confuse Patachitra (cloth scroll, Odisha) with Madhubani (wall painting, Bihar).

questions.stem: 'Dhokra' — non-ferrous metal casting using the lost-wax technique with tribal aesthetics — is most famously practiced in:

options.option_text: Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha (tribal belt)

questions.explanation: Dhokra (also Dokra) — 4,000-year-old lost-wax bronze casting tradition. The famous 'Dancing Girl' of Mohenjodaro (~2500 BCE) was made by this technique. Process: clay core → wax model → covered in clay mold → fire melts wax out (lost wax) → molten bronze poured in → break mold to retrieve casting. Rural artisan communities — Ojha (Chhattisgarh), Sithulias (WB) — preserve the craft. GI tags: Dokra (Chhattisgarh), Bankura Dokra (WB).

questions.stem: 'Kovalam' is to brass-engraved art-pieces as 'Aranmula' is to:

options.option_text: Metal mirrors made from a special tin-copper alloy

questions.explanation: Aranmula Kannadi — handmade metal-alloy MIRROR from Aranmula, Pathanamthitta, Kerala. Made of a secret alloy (mostly tin + copper) polished without any silvering — reflects the 'true' image (no glass distortion). Considered one of the eight auspicious items in a Kerala bride's trousseau. GI tag 2005 — India's 2nd GI. Recipe is closely guarded by a few families. Time-consuming — 3-15 days per mirror. Not 'Kovalam' (that's a beach in TVM); confusable trap.
